newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INTERVIEW-NatMut urges caution on China.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-NatMut urges caution on China.

text.p: Australian life office National Mutual Holdings Ltd on Friday urged caution after announcing its parent, Axa-UAP, would be allowed to operate in China, saying a licence could take up to 18 months to be granted.
"I express caution to everyone because there's nothing guaranteed here," National Mutual managing director Geoff Tomlinson told Reuters.
"No-one should get excited about it today. It's good news for the Axa group, but there's a lot of water to go under the bridge yet," he added
Earlier, National Mutual announced its French parent had been told verbally by Chinese authorities that it would receive a life insurance licence.
National Mutual shares jumped on the news.

But Tomlinson said the conditions of the licence had yet to been made clear, though Axa-UAP planned to hand the management of the business to National Mutual Asia and its joint venture partner China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd.
National Mutual Holdings, owned 51 percent by Axa-UAP, is effectively the Asian arm of the giant French insurer.
Tomlinson cited the experience of Canadian insurer Manulife, which finally received its China licence 18 months after Chinese authorities indicated it would be able to operate there.
Axa-UAP would become only the fourth foreign life insurer permitted to operate in China, he said.
